title: Augmentation projections of weighted subset-partition sums
statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set, $X$ a set, and $V_n$ the free abelian group on symbols $[x,I]$ with $x\in X$, $I\subseteq E$ and $|I|=n$, for $n\geq0$, extended by zero for $n<0$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. For each subset $A\subseteq E$ choose a function $t_A:X\to X$ with $t_\varnothing=\mathrm{id}_X$. For every ordered pair of disjoint subsets choose an integer $c(A,B)$ such that $c(\varnothing,I)=c(I,\varnothing)=1$. In the total graded tensor group $T_n=\bigoplus_{a+b=n}V_a\otimes_{\mathbf Z}V_b$, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], define the degree-preserving homomorphism
$$P[x,I]=\sum_{A\sqcup B=I}c(A,B)[x,A]\otimes[t_A(x),B].$$
Let $e:V\to\mathbf Z[0]$ be $e[x,\varnothing]=1$ in degree zero and zero in all other degrees. Here $\mathbf Z[0]$ is $\mathbf Z$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere. The canonical graded unit maps
$$U_L:\mathbf Z[0]\otimes V\longrightarrow V,\quad n\otimes z\longmapsto nz,\qquad U_R:V\otimes\mathbf Z[0]\longrightarrow V,\quad z\otimes n\longmapsto nz$$
are isomorphisms with inverses $z\mapsto1\otimes z$ and $z\mapsto z\otimes1$. The projections of $P$ satisfy, on every generator,
$$(e\otimes1)P[x,I]=1\otimes[x,I],\qquad(1\otimes e)P[x,I]=[x,I]\otimes1.$$
In the first projection all terms with $A\ne\varnothing$ vanish; in the second all terms with $B\ne\varnothing$ vanish. Under $\mathbf Z\otimes\mathbf Z\cong\mathbf Z$, the double projection is
$$(e\otimes e)P[x,I]=\begin{cases}1&I=\varnothing,\\0&I\ne\varnothing.\end{cases}$$
In particular $U_L(e\otimes1)P=1_V=U_R(1\otimes e)P$ and $(e\otimes e)P=e$ as graded homomorphisms.
If $d_n:V_n\to V_{n-1}$ makes $V$ a chain complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] and $e_0d_1=0$, equip tensors with $d_T(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^a x\otimes dy$ for $x\in V_a$. Then $e$, $e\otimes1$, $1\otimes e$, $e\otimes e$, and the unit isomorphisms $U_L,U_R$ and their inverses commute with the differentials. No assertion that $P$ commutes with $d$ is assumed or made. These statements also hold when $E$ or $X$ is empty. If $E=\varnothing$ and $X=\{x\}$, then $V_0\cong\mathbf Z$ by $[x,\varnothing]\mapsto1$, all positive degrees vanish, and $P(1)=1\otimes1$.

proof.text: Each $I$ has finitely many ordered disjoint partitions: choose $A\subseteq I$ and put $B=I\setminus A$. Each summand of $P[x,I]$ has degree $|A|+|B|=|I|$. By the finite-basis-expansion definition in [def-weil-pbc-free-module], extending this prescription to a finite integral linear combination defines a unique homomorphism in each degree. The same argument defines $e$, and all maps from negative source degrees are zero.

proof.text: By the bilinear universal property of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], $(m,z)\mapsto mz$ and $(z,m)\mapsto mz$ induce $U_L,U_R$. The maps $z\mapsto1\otimes z$ and $z\mapsto z\otimes1$ are linear by bilinearity. Their composites with the unit maps are identities because $1z=z$, $1\otimes(mz)=m\otimes z$, and $(mz)\otimes1=z\otimes m$. Pure tensors generate, so these are inverse homomorphisms. Only degree-zero unit factors are nonzero, giving the graded assertions.

proof.text: Apply $e\otimes1$ termwise, using bilinearity from [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. If $A\ne\varnothing$, then $e[x,A]=0$. The only surviving partition is $(\varnothing,I)$, whose coefficient is $1$ and whose second factor is $[t_\varnothing(x),I]=[x,I]$. Its image is $1\otimes[x,I]$. Applying $U_L$ gives $[x,I]$. Equality on all generators extends to $U_L(e\otimes1)P=1_V$ by [def-weil-pbc-free-module].

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written elementary algebra below the tame-boundary route; the blueprint paragraph itself contains no partition-diagonal formula.

proof.text: For $1\otimes e$ the terms with $B\ne\varnothing$ vanish. The surviving partition $(I,\varnothing)$ has coefficient $1$, and $e[t_I(x),\varnothing]=1$ regardless of $t_I(x)$. Thus its image is $[x,I]\otimes1$, and $U_R$ gives $[x,I]$. For $e\otimes e$, both parts must be empty: this is impossible unless $I=\varnothing$, when the unique term gives $1\otimes1$, identified with $1$. Bilinearity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and basis expansion [def-weil-pbc-free-module] give both homomorphism equalities.

proof.text: Assume now the differential hypotheses. The equation for a chain map in [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology] gives $ed=0=d e$: the target $\mathbf Z[0]$ has zero differential, and $e_{n-1}d_n$ is zero unless $n=1$, where it is the assumed $e_0d_1=0$. This includes $n=0$ since $V_{-1}=0$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written elementary algebra below the tame-boundary route; the blueprint paragraph itself contains no partition-diagonal formula.

proof.text: For homogeneous $x\in V_a$, $y\in V_b$, the stated tensor differential squares to $d^2x\otimes y+((-1)^{a-1}+(-1)^a)dx\otimes dy+x\otimes d^2y=0$. Terms containing $dx$ vanish at $a=0$. Thus it defines a complex by [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Its formula is well-defined by bilinearity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and extends from pure tensors to finite sums in the graded direct sum.

proof.text: Put $L=e\otimes1$. On $x\otimes y$ of bidegree $(a,b)$, $Ld_T(x\otimes y)=e(dx)\otimes y+(-1)^a e(x)\otimes dy$. The first term is zero by step 5. For $a>0$, $e(x)=0$; for $a=0$, the sign is $1$, so the remaining term is exactly $dL(x\otimes y)$. For $R=1\otimes e$, $Rd_T(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes e(y)+(-1)^a x\otimes e(dy)=dx\otimes e(y)=dR(x\otimes y)$. Here step 5 kills $e(dy)$, and the target unit differential is zero. Pure tensors generate [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], so both are chain maps in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written elementary algebra below the tame-boundary route; the blueprint paragraph itself contains no partition-diagonal formula.

proof.text: For the double projection, applying $e\otimes e$ to $d_T(x\otimes y)$ gives $e(dx)\otimes e(y)+(-1)^a e(x)\otimes e(dy)=0$ by step 5, as required for its zero-differential target. For the unit maps and inverses, the four equations are $U_Ld(m\otimes z)=m\,dz=d(mz)$, $U_Rd(z\otimes m)=m\,dz=d(mz)$, $d(1\otimes z)=1\otimes dz$, and $d(z\otimes1)=dz\otimes1$. Thus all commute with differentials; generation by pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives the equations on the whole modules, exactly the chain-map criterion [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology].

source.place: Paragraph (3), open direct image: agent-written elementary algebra below the tame-boundary route; the blueprint paragraph itself contains no partition-diagonal formula.

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, every free module is zero by [def-weil-pbc-free-module], so the identities hold on the zero groups. If $E=\varnothing$, only $I=\varnothing$ occurs, so all positive degrees vanish and its unique partition gives $P[x,\varnothing]=[x,\varnothing]\otimes[x,\varnothing]$. For $X=\{x\}$, the basis identification $[x,\varnothing]\mapsto1$ gives $V_0\cong\mathbf Z$ and $P(1)=1\otimes1$. No step requires $P$ to commute with the differentials.
